---
title: "User guide"
---

The guide follows the path from raw observations to a possession-level risk profile. All examples use observed match data and the models distributed with PRESS.

1. **[Dataset and preprocessing](data.qmd).** Understand the ten-match source dataset, preprocess one match and inspect the input-table contract.
2. **[Possession segmentation and context](vignettes/setup/possession_and_checkpoint_setup.ipynb).** Define individual possessions, canonical actions and checkpoints, additional snapshots, start type and previous action, and the labels used by the learned models.
3. **[Installation and use](vignettes/00_match_workflow/00_match_workflow.ipynb).** Install PRESS, load a real match, select Vujica’s possession, inspect its frames and checkpoints, calculate the possession-loss hazard h and the expected loss xLoss, and save and reload the results.

To run the example, first install PRESS with the commands in part 3. Download the original SkillCorner match files and follow part 3: `PRESS.from_skillcorner(...)` prepares the required inputs in memory. For already prepared tables from another source, use `PRESS(...)` directly and call the separate segmentation function when needed.

The four-part [reference](api.qmd) documents individual classes and functions: [initialization](api.qmd), [solvers](solvers.qmd), [getters](reference/getters.qmd) and [plots](reference/plots.qmd). The [model pages](index.qmd#models) explain the mathematical components; the [benchmarks](benchmark.qmd) describe their training and held-out evaluation.

[Models, calculation configurations and frame results](api.qmd#model-configuration-result) explains where fitted coefficients, spline designs, physical settings and predictions are stored, with ball-drive, pitch-control and BCOS examples.
